Playbook.name: AD — Password Spraying: Single Source Failing Against Many Distinct Accounts - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: One source IP failed authentication (4625/4771) against 12 or more distinct accounts within 30 minutes. The triage question: is this an attacker walking the user list with a few passwords, or an internal system (patching, monitoring, mis-scoped job) authenticating with stale credentials on many hosts?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A successful spray yields a valid credential without lockouts, giving initial access that blends into normal logon traffic in a banking domain.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

Signal.Name: Spray shape
Signal.Details: source.ip with >= 12 distinct target users failing inside the rule window; DNS/core relays 192.168.25.1/.2 and 172.17.25.1 are excluded by the rule.

Input.name: $source_ip
Input.description: Source IP from the alert (threshold group key).

ImmediateCapture.Item: Alert window user cardinality from kibana.alert.threshold_result

InitialAssessment.Rule: If the source is a known management/patching server AND every failure is the SAME error for the SAME few service accounts, lean Misconfiguration.
If failures cover many human accounts with rotating usernames and there is ANY success from the same source, escalate immediately.

Investigation.Goal: Decide whether $source_ip performed a deliberate multi-account credential attack, and whether it obtained a valid credential.

Step.name: Profile the failing accounts from this source
Step.Purpose: Establish breadth and error mix: many users each with 1-3 failures = spray; a few service accounts failing continuously = credential loop.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE source.ip == "$source_ip" AND event.code IN ("4625","4771") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL status = COALESCE(winlog.event_data.Status, "-"), sub = COALESCE(winlog.event_data.SubStatus, "-") | STATS fails = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), codes = VALUES(event.code), errors = VALUES(CONCAT(status, "/", sub)) BY winlog.event_data.TargetUserName | SORT fails DESC | LIMIT 100
Step.AnalystNotes: Spray: 12+ users, low per-user counts, mostly 0xC000006A/0x18 (wrong password). Loop: 1-3 accounts, hundreds of identical failures over hours. 0xC0000064 (user does not exist) with rotating names = username enumeration.

Step.name: Check for ANY successful logon from the same source
Step.Purpose: A success from the spraying source after failures is the difference between attempted and successful credential access.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE source.ip == "$source_ip" AND event.code == "4624" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS logons = COUNT(*), first_success = MIN(@timestamp), types = VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType), hosts = VALUES(host.name) BY winlog.event_data.TargetUserName | SORT logons DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: Compare first_success against the failure window from INV-01: a success DURING or AFTER the spray for an account that was being sprayed is strong TP evidence. Machine accounts (name$) logging on are normal.

Step.name: Measure target breadth across hosts/DCs
Step.Purpose: Distinguish a source hammering one system (app loop) from one walking many targets (attack infrastructure).
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE source.ip == "$source_ip" AND event.code IN ("4625","4771") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS fails = COUNT(*), users = COUNT_DISTINCT(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName) BY host.name | SORT fails DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: One receiving host + few users = broken client on/behind that host. Many DCs receiving many users = domain-wide spray.

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows a successful 4624 for a HUMAN account that INV-01 shows was failing from the same source during the window.
Node.Result: True Positive (Credential Compromised - escalate to IR immediately)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows 12+ distinct mostly-human accounts with low per-user failure counts and no success; source is not an approved scanner/management host.
Node.Result: True Positive (Spray Attempted, No Success confirmed)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows 1-3 service/application accounts failing repeatedly with identical errors for hours from an application server (compare with the JCB known-loop set: aml_srv, achuser, ksnproxy, oper, callcenter accounts).
Source is the documented Nessus scanner 192.168.166.1 or an approved auth-audit job with a change record.
Breadth is borderline (mixed service+human accounts) or the source cannot be identified from CMDB/ownership.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-SPRAY-PROFILE, INV-02-SPRAY-SUCCESS, INV-03-SPRAY-TARGETS to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: An approved scanner or auth-audit tool authenticated against many accounts by design.

Indicators.Item: Source is 192.168.166.1 (Nessus) or another documented assessment host.
Failures align exactly with a scheduled scan window.
Error mix is uniform and no success follows.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the scan schedule with vulnerability management.
Propose a rule exception for the scanner source only.

TruePositive.Definition: A deliberate multi-account credential-guessing campaign from one source.

Indicators.Item: Many distinct human accounts, each with a small number of wrong-password failures in minutes.
Username enumeration signature: 0xC0000064 on nonexistent, alphabetically or list-ordered names.
Any success from the same source for a sprayed account (upgrade to compromise).

SOCAction.Item: Block or isolate the source at the switch/firewall.
Force password reset + session revocation for any account with a success.
Open an incident and pull the source system for forensics if internal.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An internal system authenticating with wrong/stale credentials on a loop - operational, not malicious.

Indicators.Item: Same 1-3 service accounts failing continuously with identical Status/SubStatus for hours or days.
Source is an application/management server (JCB known loops: AML app servers 192.168.228.x -> aml_srv, achuser, ksnproxy).
No human accounts touched and no successes.

SOCAction.Item: Open a ticket with the application owner to fix the stored credential.
Track under the P0 credential-hygiene program; do NOT exception the rule (fix the source).

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Check INV-02 accounts for active sessions and revoke.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Reset passwords for accounts with post-spray successes.
Forensic triage of the source host if internal (what process is authenticating).

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Add the confirmed-loop sources to the credential-hygiene remediation list.

QualityChecks.Check: Rule excludes DNS relays (192.168.25.1/.2, 172.17.25.1) - confirm these are still the relay IPs.
Null-source interactive failures are NOT visible to this rule; the callcenter/branch storm is tracked separately.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Scan schedule verified with the owning team and matches the alert window.
No success events from the source in INV-02.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Compromised accounts reset and sessions revoked.
Source contained and root process identified.
